column1: # The common subset of ECMA-262 and POSIX ERE an argument.pattern is written
# in (agent-cli/v2 2.3), as src/pattern.c reads and matches it and as
# python/maelys_cli.py checks it and hands it to `re`. Read by
# tests/test_pattern.c and python/tests/test_maelys_cli.py: the two sides
# answer every line alike, which is what holds C and Python to one reading.

column3: ok|refused        -- the pattern is in the subset, or not

column4: yes|no    -- the value matches, a search as regexec()

column1: #                                   and re.search() make it; in VALUE, \n
#                                   is a newline and \\ a backslash
# The patterns the products declare today.
# Outside the subset: not a pattern at all.
# Outside the subset: a bound POSIX does not guarantee, or malformed.
# Outside the subset: a quantifier on nothing, two in a row, a lazy one, an anchor.
# Outside the subset: the groups ECMA-262 names and POSIX ERE lacks, back-references.
# Outside the subset: escapes that are not of a metacharacter.
# Outside the subset: what the two dialects read differently in a bracket expression.
# Outside the subset: empty alternatives and groups, which POSIX leaves undefined.
# Outside what this reader bounds: 33 nested groups, 130050 states.
# Matches: a search, anchors at the ends of the value, `.` not a newline,
# An anchor inside a group is an anchor: cd$ holds at the end of the value
# only, and nothing then follows it. glibc answers yes to the first line.
